latest_release.name: Lichii nx2 build 177 (87d84d5)
latest_release.body:
## Changes since build 160

Built from nx2 87d84d513c. Build 160 was 2eb5f08. That's 86 merged changes.

> **The yuzu name is gone.** The build system, source folders, Qt frontend, translations, emulator libraries and docs now say Lichii instead of the name inherited from yuzu. Your settings, saves and shader caches are kept: config keys, data folders and cache formats don't change, and the few on-disk names that still carry the old name (the shader cache's file magic, the save-size file inside saves, the import path for yuzu data) stay as they are. The program files are still called `lichii`, `eden-cli` and `eden-room`. On macOS the app's bundle id changed, so macOS asks for camera and input permission again (#1541, #1550, #1551, #1552, #1553, #1544, #1582).

### Big fixes
- **Ocarina of Time: the far forest no longer floats, and Hyrule Field's frame rate is back.** In test builds after build 160, the far pine forest in Hyrule Field and in Kakariko at night was drawn unculled and partly above the ridge, and a spot that ran at 40 fps dropped to 27 fps (RTX 3080). An upstream change that came in with the Eglantine sync (#1462) generated the shader helpers for these foliage programs in a form NVIDIA's compiler mishandles. They're generated the previous way again, which also gives up the cold-compile time upstream saved on them (#1539).
- **Orbitals no longer freezes after the Unreal logo.** It froze at 0 fps on every Lichii build so far, because vi2 command 53, which Unreal uses to see which frames were shown, had no handler. This covers Orbitals and the Global Friends Pass. Ported from ghzeni's #742 (#1590).
- **Booting a second game without restarting Lichii no longer crashes.** A GPU channel still waiting on a semaphore when a game stopped left a stale entry behind, and the next game's GPU thread read the stopped game's freed memory. It was seen when booting Donkey Kong Bananza after stopping Ocarina of Time (#1592).
- **Stopping a game no longer ends in a "Userspace PANIC".** Guest threads kept running while services stopped replying, so about half of all stopped Ocarina of Time sessions logged a panic (2010-0212) that looked like a crash. Guest threads are now suspended before the system powers off (#1450).
- **Ocarina of Time: the dark grid over water is gone.** Boxy dark squares followed Link over water whenever a light such as Navi, an enemy or a rupee was near. Shadow maps from the game's light table are now bound through descriptor arrays. Testers on an RX 7800 XT, RTX 4090 and RTX 5080 confirmed it. Port of jpkto's #354, with his commits kept (#1485).
- **Ocarina of Time: a likely fix for the GPU hang after long play.** 38 OoT sessions from 28 players ended in a device loss after long play, on AMD, RADV and NVIDIA. A native task shader could launch a leftover, huge number of mesh workgroups; it now sets that count to zero first. Ported from SethRamey's upstream fix. It can't be confirmed yet: the hang shows up about 0.05 to 0.2 times per hour of play (#1492).
- **Mario Kart World: the hang while loading is fixed.** Two GPU threads and a guest core deadlocked. The GPU threads no longer wait on kernel locks for sparse memory: a background thread prepares memory ahead of time, and writes are kept until it's ready. The memory reserve follows godpow's upstream design (#1413).
- **Yoshi and the Mysterious Book (demo): no more memory runaway.** The demo remaps the same memory every frame, each remap got a new device address, and one buffer kept growing until the process ran out of memory. Freed device ranges of the same size are now reused. In a 150 s run the buffer cache peaked at 308 MiB instead of 2,025 MiB, and the process at 4.7 GB instead of 14.7 GB (#1528). A follow-up gives the kept ranges back when device space runs out, so allocations of other sizes don't fail (#1532).
- **Games no longer vanish from the list when keys are missing.** Switch 1 NSP, NSZ, XCI and XCZ files that can't be decrypted are listed with "Decr
